title: Crestline Fleet Account Make-Good Line on Tire Pricing Corrections
content:
On a Crestline Fleet Account, a pricing correction on a tire invoice posted with no fleet discount carries a make-good line, which depends on the tire set bought on the ticket.

## Make-good line

| Tire set bought on the ticket | Make-good line added to the correction |
|---|---|
| four or more tires | the mounting and balancing of every tire on the set is added to the correction: the set's tire count times its line's mount-and-balance charge per tire |
| one to three tires | one tenth (10 percent) of the restored discount is added, rounded half up to the cent |
| no tire set bought on the ticket | nothing is added |

The tire set bought on the ticket is the Tire Sets & Treadwear Limited Warranty set recorded for the invoice's vehicle with a purchase date equal to the invoice date; its tire count and the mount-and-balance charge per tire of its tire line are read from that product's records.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

- A set of 4 tires on a line with a mount-and-balance charge of 20.00 per tire: make-good line 80.00.
- A set of 2 tires, restored discount 31.25: one tenth is 3.125, rounded half up to 3.13.
- No set recorded for the vehicle on the invoice date: nothing is added.

## Where the amount sits

Because a fleet invoice posted without the program discount is Crestline's billing error, make-good amounts are added to the pricing correction on a tire invoice that an account invoiced without sales tax received with no fleet discount at all. The correction starts from the restored discount (the fleet discount the ticket should have carried less the discount the invoice already carried). The limit of the invoice amount less the credit memos and early-pay discounts already on the invoice is applied last, after every make-good amount, and prevails over every other part of the correction rule, so a correction can fall below the restored discount only when that limit is lower; the correction is rounded half up to the cent once, after the limit.
